A signed-in non-subscriber picks $14 per month or $143 per year on `/subscribe` and reaches Stripe Checkout for that plan. Card SBS5 (SB10).

## Acceptance criteria

* `/subscribe` shows "$14 per month" and "$143 per year", a "Subscribe monthly" button, then a "Subscribe yearly" button (SB10).
* Subscribe yearly opens Stripe Checkout for `STRIPE_YEARLY_PRICE_ID`; Subscribe monthly for `STRIPE_PRICE_ID`. The server maps the plan name to the price; the browser never sends a price id.
* The app refuses to start without `STRIPE_YEARLY_PRICE_ID`; `.env.example` lists it after `STRIPE_PRICE_ID` (SB10).
* A yearly subscriber counts as subscribed and opens the customer portal from "Manage subscription", like a monthly one (SB10).

## Notes

* Criterion 4 needs no code: `isSubscribed` reads only `status`; the webhook stores status and `items.data[0].current_period_end` for any price (`app/src/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts`); `openPortal` sends only `stripeCustomerId` (`app/src/app/actions/billing.ts`).
* Replaces NEB-1744's single "Subscribe" button with the two buttons above.
* Not in this story: the daily model-cost cap (SB11), portal plan switching (a Stripe dashboard setting).
EOF

S={repo}/.compose/stripe-billing/scratch/stripe-billing-planner; cat > $S/stories.md <<'EOF'
## Proposed stories

Create these four stories, in ship order, on the product owner's go.

**SBS1. Subscription seam for the recommender** (ships first; NEB-1733 codes against it)
* A `Subscription` table, one-to-one with `User` (SB7), created by one migration; deleting a user deletes its row.
* `SubscriptionService.isSubscribed(userId)` is true when the user's row has status `active` or `trialing` (SB6).
* It is false for any other status and when the user has no row.

**SBS2. Subscribe through Stripe Checkout**
* A signed-in user without an active subscription who opens `/` lands on `/subscribe` (SB2).
* `/subscribe` shows "$14 per month", a Subscribe button, and a "Fair use applies" link to a short explanation; a subscriber who opens it lands on `/`.
* Subscribe opens Stripe Checkout for `STRIPE_PRICE_ID` in subscription mode, tagged with the user's id; Cancel returns to `/subscribe`.
* Back from a paid Checkout before the webhook lands, `/subscribe` shows "Payment received" and a "Check again" link instead of the Subscribe button, so nobody pays twice.
* The app refuses to start without `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_PRICE_ID`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; `.env.example` lists them (SB3).
Built on unconfirmed: SB9 (the fair-use copy follows option A).

**SBS3. Webhook stores the subscription**
* `POST /api/stripe/webhook` with a missing or invalid signature returns 400 and writes nothing.
* A signed `customer.subscription.created`, `.updated`, or `.deleted` event saves the user's customer id, subscription id, status, and period end; a replay updates the same row.
* Any other event, or one without a user id in its metadata, returns 200 and writes nothing.
* After a paid Checkout the user reaches the signed-in home.

**SBS4. Manage subscription in the Stripe portal**
* A subscriber's signed-in home shows a "Manage subscription" button above Sign out.
* It opens the Stripe customer portal for their customer, returning to `/`.
* A user with no subscription row who triggers it lands on `/subscribe`.
EOF

## Design facts

* Stripe keys come from env (`env.ts`); `app/.env` holds the test keys (SB8).
* Checkout and portal URLs are built from the request's `Origin` header; Next.js checks it against the host for server actions.
* The webhook upserts the event's subscription state by `metadata.userId`; out-of-order events are accepted.
* Checkout passes `customer_email` and never reuses a Stripe customer.
* Buttons are plain form posts with no pending or error state in this slice.
* Stripe SDK 23 (API `2026-09-30.endive`): the period end is `items.data[0].current_period_end`, not on the subscription.

## Outside waits

* SB8 settled: the product owner puts the three test values in `app/.env`. Implementers mock Stripe; nothing waits on the keys.
* The Stripe dashboard needs a webhook endpoint for `customer.subscription.created`, `.updated`, `.deleted`, and the customer portal turned on in test mode.
* A local e2e of the webhook needs the Stripe CLI (`stripe listen`); it is not installed on this machine.
* SB9 (fair use) is open; tasks 006 and 007 carry the option-A copy.
